question: Estimate the number of petrol pumps in India.

answer.counts: Retail fuel outlets (forecourts) selling petrol or diesel to the public

alternatives.definition: Including captive pumps for railways, defence and fleet depots

assumptions: All of India, all oil companies, public and private.
Small rural outlets (Kisan Seva Kendras) are included.
Standalone CNG stations and EV chargers are excluded.
Fuel volumes are for a financial year, April to March.

bands.note: Proposed from the two blind solvers in the format stress test. Under 30,000 usually means peak capacity was used; over 200,000 usually means nozzles were counted. To be replaced or checked by the calculated range from #50.

real_figure.source: PPAC (Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell), as reported by Deccan Chronicle
real_figure.note: The network crossed 1 lakh outlets in November 2025 and has roughly doubled in a decade, so older figures are much lower.

known_bias: Sound estimates land below the real figure, because people assume an average pump is busier than it is. India has many small rural outlets selling far less than a city or highway pump, so real average throughput is nearer 120 to 140 KL a month.

provenance.review_notes: Diesel consumption is marked as an assumption until a PPAC figure is checked.

catches: Units to align: fuel in tonnes against throughput in litres, and monthly throughput against annual volume

paths.name: Fuel volume divided by throughput per pump
steps: Convert petrol tonnes to litres at 0.74 kg per litre
Convert diesel tonnes to litres at 0.83 kg per litre, then keep the share sold at pumps
Add the two for retail litres a year
Annual throughput per pump = monthly throughput x 12
Pumps = retail litres a year / annual throughput per pump

drivers.name: Share of diesel sold at pumps

paths.model_solution: 40 million tonnes of petrol is about 54 billion litres. 90 million tonnes of diesel is about 108 billion litres, of which about 88% is sold at pumps, so 95 billion. Retail volume is about 150 billion litres a year. An average pump sells 150 KL a month, or 1.8 million litres a year, so India needs about 83,000 pumps.
catches: Tonnes must be converted to litres, at different densities for petrol and diesel
Some diesel goes in bulk to railways, defence and industry and never reaches a pump
Average throughput is far below a busy city or highway pump
common_mistakes: Using a busy urban pump's throughput as the national average
Counting petrol only and forgetting diesel, which is twice the volume
paths.sanity_check: About 83,000 pumps for 1.4 billion people is 1 per 17,000 people, plausible given India's low car ownership.

paths.name: Refuels per day divided by refuels one pump handles
steps: Active vehicles by type = registered vehicles x share still in use
Refuels per day = active vehicles of each type / days between refuels
Refuels one pump handles a day = litres sold a day / average litres per refuel
Pumps = refuels per day / refuels per pump per day
paths.model_solution: About 230 million vehicles in use. Two-wheelers refuel every 5 days, cars weekly, three-wheelers and trucks every day or two, for about 45 million refuels a day. A pump selling 5,000 litres a day at about 8 litres a refuel handles about 650 refuels. 45 million / 650 is about 70,000 pumps.
catches: Registered vehicles overstate the vehicles in use, because scrapped vehicles are rarely deregistered
Two-wheelers dominate the number of refuels but not the litres
common_mistakes: Treating every registered vehicle as active
Using a pump's peak capacity instead of its average use
paths.sanity_check: 650 refuels at 8 litres is about 5,200 litres a day, or 156 KL a month, which should match path 1's throughput.

paths.name: Coverage: urban density plus rural spacing
paths.no_archetype_reason: The count comes from how far apart pumps must be for access, not from fuel demand or pump capacity.
paths.base: Urban population and the rural land area that needs serving
steps: Urban pumps = urban population / people per urban pump
Rural pumps = rural area served / area one rural pump covers
paths.model_solution: 500 million urban people at 1 pump per 15,000 is about 33,000. About 2.5 million square kilometres of served rural land at 1 pump per 55 square kilometres is about 45,000. Total about 80,000.
catches: Highway pumps can be counted twice, as highway and as rural
Rural pumps are partly set by policy, so pure demand logic undercounts them
common_mistakes: Using India's total land area, including desert, forest and mountain
Applying one urban density to the whole country
paths.sanity_check: Explains why the real count is higher than paths 1 and 2: many rural pumps exist for access, not volume.
